entry.title: C++26 Ranges: Better Infrastructure
entry.summary: C++26 ranges isn’t only about new view adaptors. Three changes landed that don’t give you new ways to compose pipelines but fix real problems: containers can now reserve space for lazy ranges that don’t know their exact size, <random> finally works with ranges, and ranges::to no longer forces you into a | pipeline when a simple function call would do. approximately_sized_range and rese...

entry.title: C++26 Ranges: Four New Views
entry.summary: C++20 shipped a powerful ranges library, but the set of view adaptors had some obvious gaps. Want to get the output as a container? No luck. At least C++23 helped with that. Want to iterate over two vectors as one sequence? Write your own. Want to avoid redundant evaluations in a transform | filter pipeline? Write a workaround.
